source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It is primarily a disciplinary tool used to identify staff who do not meet productivity expectations","B":"It is intended to replace adequate staffing, communication, leadership, and other work-environment needs","C":"It should be reserved for executives because peer and bedside recognition have no professional value","D":"It reinforces the value of contributions and can support fulfillment, morale, and retention efforts"}}
source_row.rationale: AACN identifies meaningful recognition as one of six standards for healthy work environments. Recognition systems should acknowledge contributions in ways meaningful to staff and are linked with fulfillment and retention-focused workplace efforts.
source_row.source_detail: Healthy Work Environment standard and critical elements for organizational recognition systems; current page accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: Why is meaningful staff recognition included in healthy nursing work-environment standards?
